note: Synthetic persona output. These are hypotheses, not evidence. Task 1 was written after reading only WORLD.md, before opening the designs.
replay_predictions: Framing step: I answer it on my phone within a few hours, but loosely. I'd write 'objective = more sales', 'budget = the Google budget I already have, maybe a bit more' and 'horizon = next month, before the Q4/Eid toy season'. I would NOT give a number for budget or target ROAS, because I don't think in those terms. If it gives me 3 preset choices to tap, I pick one in 30 seconds.

C3 (delivery promises) and C7 (reallocate at flat budget): I answer both the same day from memory in one 2-minute reply, e.g. 'free delivery over 150, same-day if ordered before 2pm in Dubai, no Sunday dispatch, no click-and-collect' and 'yes, move money around, just don't spend more'. My answers are mostly right but not precise: the cut-off is different for Abu Dhabi and I forget to mention that.

C5 (fake scarcity counters): I answer fast but defensively, something like 'the stock counter app helps conversion, why remove it?'. I probably say 'ok to test removing it' only if the consultant explains why. The word 'fake' annoys me a little.

C1 and C2 (WhatsApp): I can't answer these myself. I forward the text to my sales lead on WhatsApp, and it takes 1–2 days. What comes back is partial: 'we use WhatsApp Business app on 2 phones, about 30–50 chats a day, replies within an hour in shop hours, nobody answers at night'. Nobody knows the opted-in or reachable count or whether broadcast is allowed. Those stay blank or end up as a guess.

C4 (Odoo export): this is the one most likely to be delayed or come back wrong. I don't know what 'PORTAL' means here, and exports are exactly what I hate. I ask my accountant or ops person, and it takes 2–3 days. When it arrives it is probably the wrong report: invoices instead of sales orders, missing phone numbers, or a pivot instead of raw lines. Or I reply 'can't you just connect to Odoo / Shopify yourself?'.

Google Ads script/xlsx: I won't run a script. I'd say 'I'll add you as a user on the Ads account' or 'give me a Connect Google button'. If neither is possible it stalls for a week while I wait for my agency or freelancer, who manages the ads, to do it.
C6 (go/no-go on '4 parked items'): I don't remember what the 4 items are, so I either ignore it or reply 'which ones?'. It adds a round trip.

My goal drifts and the scope worries me. I asked 'which Google campaign should I add?' and got questions about WhatsApp, delivery and scarcity counters. My first reaction is 'this is getting bigger than I asked'. If I don't get a quick win, like 'add a Performance Max campaign for top-20 SKUs, here's why', within about a week, I lose interest or go back to my ads agency. If it's explained in one line ('your ads bring chats your team doesn't answer at night, so more ads = wasted spend'), I accept the wider scope and actually get more interested.

K_problems.problem: 25 required fields, all mandatory, can't save part-way
K_problems.why: I have 15 minutes on a phone. I will be interrupted halfway and lose everything. I'd quit on the first screen.

K_problems.problem: Fields like Mission, Vision, ISIC code, Risk appetite 1–10, Preferred methodology
K_problems.why: I don't know my ISIC code and I have no 'preferred methodology'. These are consultant words, and they make me feel the tool isn't for me. They are irrelevant to 'which campaign should I add'.

K_problems.problem: Trade licence number and legal name required up front
K_problems.why: Feels like bureaucracy before I've seen any value. I'd have to dig out documents, and it's a trust and privacy concern too.

K_problems.problem: 3 KPIs/constraints each with unit and horizon, forced
K_problems.why: I don't have 3 constraints ready. I'd type rubbish just to get past it, which makes the analysis worse.

K_problems.problem: Data owner and decision owner emails required
K_problems.why: I am both, or it's my sales lead for WhatsApp. It isn't clear what happens if I put a staff email in. Will they get spammed?
Internal system jargon. I don't know what any of it means.

K_problems.problem: Gap list uses codes like gap_01 sales_tx, cust_master, mkt_spend_ts, 'provenance class: observed'
K_problems.why: I can't tell what file to give you. Say 'Your Shopify orders, last 12 months', not 'sales_tx'.

K_problems.problem: Red/green dots with no text for status
K_problems.why: I don't know whether red means missing, wrong or urgent. Green on cust_master: did I upload that? It's unclear and wouldn't work for colour-blind users.

K_problems.problem: No reason given for each data item
K_problems.why: I won't spend time on an export if I don't know why you need it.
I don't know how to pull this from Odoo or Shopify. I'd give up or send the wrong thing.
I'm on my phone most of the time, and you can't drag files on a phone. Blocking.
Connecting Google or Shopify is the one thing I'm happy to do. Manual uploads are what I hate.

K_problems.problem: No 'someone else has this' or 'I don't have this' option
K_problems.why: WhatsApp data is with my sales team, and I have no way to delegate or say it doesn't exist. I'm stuck.

K_problems.problem: Upload error 'Error 422: schema mismatch' toast for 3 seconds
K_problems.why: Meaningless to me, and it vanishes before I've read it. It doesn't tell me which column is wrong or show an example, so I'd re-upload the same file and fail again.

K_problems.problem: Session expires after 10 minutes of inactivity
K_problems.why: I step away for a delivery issue, come back and have lost my work, especially with the unsaveable form. I'd abandon.

K_problems.problem: Status screen: 'Engagement #A7F3: processing' plus spinner only
K_problems.why: No ETA, no notification promise and no sign of whether you need anything from me. I'd keep checking, then forget it exists.

K_problems.problem: No sign of a human or consultant anywhere
K_problems.why: I don't know who is looking at my business data or whether a person checks it. Low trust.
Not essential for me, but it would help with staff who need to answer questions.

walkthrough: 1. Wizard step 1, company profile, 6 fields on phone: ~3 min. OK, but annoying to give before I've described the problem.
2. Step 2, pick 'Sales' and describe 'sales dropped 20% this quarter': ~2 min. Easy.
3. Step 3, Goals and KPIs: I pick the suggested 'Revenue growth' but I'm unsure about the target and horizon. ~3 min, first stuck point: I guess a number.

4. Step 4, Constraints and budget: I don't know what to put for 'budget'. Budget for the consultancy or for ads? Stuck point 2. I close the phone because the 15 minutes is used up. It saved as a draft, which is good.
5. Evening on laptop: step 5 review and submit, 2 min.

6. Data page: a table of datasets with templates. I'd have to reformat my data into your template, which is a manual export plus reformatting, the thing I hate most. It isn't clear which items matter most or why. Stuck point 3. I connect Shopify if it's offered, but the Odoo/WhatsApp rows sit there because I can't delegate them in the UI. I email my staff myself. 2–4 days pass.
7. Dashboard: 'Data completeness 60%, analysis 0%'. I don't know what I need to do to move it. Stuck point 4. I check it a few times, then stop opening it. This is the likely abandonment point.

8. If it finishes: a formal PDF with methodology and a confidence appendix, around 20 pages. I read the executive summary on my phone and skip the rest. Confidence in an appendix means I don't see how sure you are next to each recommendation.
C.quote: It looks professional, like something a bank would use, but I spent 20 minutes filling forms and the dashboard just gives me percentages. Tell me what to do, not how complete my data is.

walkthrough: 1. I type 'sales dropped 20% this quarter, what should I do' on my phone. 1 min. Feels natural.
2. Follow-up questions one at a time, ~6–8 messages over ~8 min. I answer fast, but I get interrupted mid-conversation and come back hours later.
3. Summary card: I tap [That's right] in 1 min. I'd probably accept it without reading carefully.

4. Data requests arrive one per message with a reason, which I like. I tap Connect for Google Ads and Shopify, 3 min each. Odoo export and WhatsApp numbers: I tap 'I don't have this' or plan to forward it to staff, but there's no button to invite staff into the chat, so I copy-paste to WhatsApp. Stuck point 1.

5. Two days later, after several messages, I can't remember which requests are still open. I have to scroll up the thread on my phone to find the Odoo one. Stuck point 2. Possible abandonment if the email reminder doesn't say exactly what's missing.
6. 'I'm analysing' plus an email: fine. No date given, so I wonder.

7. Report as a long chat message: the summary first is good on phone. I ask follow-ups like 'why not just discount?', which I love. But later I can't find the recommendation again in the thread to show my marketing guy. Stuck point 3. I download the PDF to share it.
A.quote: This is the easiest to start, it's just like texting. But after three days I couldn't tell what you were still waiting for from me without scrolling up forever.

walkthrough: 1. One text box: 'sales dropped 20% this quarter'. 1 min. I skip the optional upload. Then 4 short follow-ups on the same page: 4 min.

2. 'Your next step' card: 'Confirm we understood your problem (2 min)'. I read 'What we understood' and see 'other possible causes: delivery delays, fewer returning customers, ad spend shift', which is interesting. I edit one line: 2 min.
3. Next step: 'Connect Google Ads and Shopify (5 min)'. Done on phone via OAuth. 5 min. Session 1 ends at about 14 min.

4. Data checklist: Odoo export is 'Must have', with 'how to get it' steps for Odoo. I tap 'Someone else has this', invite my accountant, and it's done in 1 min. WhatsApp: invite my sales lead. This is the best part for me.

5. One small stuck point: the accountant's first upload is the wrong report, but the error explains it with an example and the accountant fixes it. I didn't have to deal with it myself. The card says 'Nothing needed from you. Results expected Thu 16 Oct', which makes me relax.

6. WhatsApp ping: 'Report ready'. On phone I read the one-paragraph answer and the steps. The 'How sure are we?' labels help: 'Strong: returning customers fell 30%' and 'Weak: ad creative fatigue, not tested'. 10 min.
7. Stuck point 2: on phone the page is long, and I scroll past the old data checklist to get to the report. I'd want the report to jump to the top once it's ready.
8. I ask a question on one finding, then send the PDF to my marketing person. Total active time ~35 min over 3–4 days.
B.quote: I always knew what you wanted from me and when I'd get the answer. And I could push the Odoo stuff to my accountant without chasing him myself. That's what I need.

interrogation.a: Being asked to do manual exports or fill long forms before I've seen any value, then losing my work when I get interrupted. If I hit that in the first 15 minutes, I'm gone and back to my ads agency.
interrogation.b: Numbers from MY data that I recognise, e.g. 'your returning customers dropped from X to Y' where I know X is right. Then 3 concrete actions for this week, each with expected impact in AED and a cost, and an honest 'how sure' label, plus a sign that a real consultant checked it. If a number looks invented or contradicts what I know, I distrust everything.
interrogation.c: For B: once the report is ready, move it to the top on mobile and collapse the completed setup sections. Add the chat-style follow-up from A ('Ask a question') as a lightweight chat panel. Make the WhatsApp notification deep-link straight to the next action. Show who has been invited and whether they've done their part, so I can see that my accountant hasn't uploaded yet. Put a 'quick win you can do today' at the very top, before the full analysis is ready.
interrogation.d: (1) An early quick win: give me 1–2 safe actions within 24 hours from the connected data alone, while waiting for the rest, so I stay engaged. (2) Let me answer questions by WhatsApp voice note or reply, since my staff live in WhatsApp. (3) A 'scope check' when the consultant widens the question beyond what I asked, e.g. 'You asked about Google campaigns; we think the bigger issue is unanswered WhatsApp chats. Continue narrow or go wide?'. (4) A follow-up after 2–4 weeks: 'did you do it, and did sales move?', which tracks results from the connected accounts automatically.
